content: **Record 3D state to compare or check your design process. ** 1. Open the History window on the left side of CLO. 2. title: How can I export FBX from CLO to APEXFiz?
content: **Question** I would like to know the recommended menu settings for FBX eport in CLO in order to use [Extract Patterns]. **Answer** [Extract Patterns] is a function that is only supported by the 3D OPTION of APEXFIz. Below is a menu of CLO software. ![FBX from CLO to APEXFiz.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40661188216601) * Select necessary avatar and patterns. * Select multiple object, not single object. Export without combining vertex * Select [Thin] for thickness. * Select default [mm] for scale. * If textures are required, select embed media. * If textures are required, enter a file name and a folder name with half-width characters. * Create a unified UV map. At this time, all pattern UVs should be arranged within the 0-1 space in the UV editor, ensuring there is no overlap. Place the pattern UVs according to the knitting direction in APEXFiz, as this direction cannot be changed in the Extract Pattern menu. Textures with alpha(hair, eyelash, etc.) may not be imported correctly. Internal lines(design lines) cannot be imported. Stitch data will not be readable in APEXFiz.
content_description: This web page provides essential menu settings for exporting FBX files from CLO to APEXFiz, specifically for utilizing the Extract Patterns feature effectively.

title: What languages does CLO come in?
content: **Question** What languages does CLO come in? **Answer** We currently offer CLO in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and much more. To change your language settings in CLO, go to Language in Settings, select the desired language, then restart the program to apply the changes. The manuals and video buttons connected within the CLO program may not be available in the set language. If you wish to change the language of the YouTube tutorial videos to your preferred language, you can first enable subtitles and then view them with automatic translation in your desired language. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/40265359237017) Additionally, you can check tutorials on the dedicated CLO YouTube channels available in Portuguese, Spanish, and Japanese. * CLO Portuguese Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOBrasil) * CLO Spanish Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOesp) * CLO Japanese Youtube: [Here](https://www.youtube.com/@CLOJapan)
content_description: Explore the diverse language options available for CLO, including instructions on changing settings and accessing tutorial resources in multiple languages.

title: Register API Plug-In
content: ### **Objective** By using [CLO API](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017616633), develop and add customized features to CLO. For example, develop a feature to collect necessary BOM information from a 3D garment produced in CLO. Then, add and use the customized feature in CLO. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ **CLO API** ** Operation** 1. Follow the path indicated below: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ **CLO API** 2. Click the ![plus_button.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360019478214) **Add** button on the right top corner. → A File Explorer dialog appears where you can search *.dll or *.dylib files. 3. Select and **Open** the desired *.dll or *.dylib file. → The Register Plug-In window appears. 4. Refer to below and configure an UI for the plug-in to be added. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Name** | Name the plug-in. **Position** | Main Menu, child menus for the selected Main Menu, and any additional corresponding child menus appear in order. Select a desired menu and choose the plug-in's position in terms of the selected menu. 5. Click **OK** to complete the registration. ※Note: * Registered plug-ins also appear in below path: Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ **Plug-in ** * Please [Contact Us,](https://www.clo3d.com/contact) if you have any questions.

title: Can I change my subscription plan?
content: **Question** Can I change my subscription plan? **Answer** You can change the plan at least 24 hours before the next bill due to your current plan. To change the subscription plan from monthly to yearly (or vice versa), 1. Sign in to the CLO web and go to the [Subscription page](https://www.clo3d.com/en/accounts/subscription). 2. Click the "Change Plan" button. 3. Check the current subscription and plan type that will be changed. 4. Click the "Change" button. *Once you change your subscription plan, you can only change the plan again ONLY AFTER you complete purchasing the product on the starting date of the changed plans. Until then, you cannot cancel the changes. Only canceling a subscription is available. *If you change the plan, you will be charged the amount for the changed plan from the next payment date of the existing plan. *If you cancel the subscription, you cannot change the plan type. *Individual plans cannot be changed as student plans and vice versa. To change your license from CLO for Individuals to CLO for Business, please reach out to CLO via [Contact Us](https://www.clo3d.com/support/contactus).
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions on how to change your subscription plan, including important guidelines and restrictions to consider before making changes.

title: Cache Animation Export
content: **Objective** Export Animation cache data. **※ Note:** You can export only the cache data of garments. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation * **Maya Cache (.mc) ** * **Maya Cache (.mcx) ** * **Point Cache 2 ** * **MDD Cache (Standard) ** * **MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max)** ** Operation** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → The Save File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. → The Export window opens. 3. Set the full details and click **OK**. **** **Object** | **Unweld/Weld Object** Export the selected objects as unweld or weld objects. **※ Note: **This option is removed from 6.2 and above. ---|--- **Unweld** Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version. | **Weld** Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. **Selected Pattern:** Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns. **Thin** Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | **Thick** Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. **Combined UV Coordinates:** Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. **※Note:** Unified Texture export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. **Scale** | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from **Unit in file to import** is selected. **Axis Conversion** | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. **Animation** | Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) | Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) **File** | **Save With Texture Files (.zip):** Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. **Save with Meta Data (.xml) :** Export the garment's pattern (Mesh), physical property, and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture:** Combine and save the garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). **Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo):** Exclude the Ambient color value when saving materials (ver2.2.0).
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions for exporting animation cache data of garments in various formats, including options for unwelding, welding, and customizing export settings.

position per Pattern or scale and rotate texture per fabric. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar or navigate to Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Texture ▶**Edit Texture (3D)** ** Translate** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=upc4EUzt7Y8 \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click and drag the texture applied to the Pattern. \- Only the texture within the selected Pattern will be moved. **Scale** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9cSa8iSQFZ8** * **Scale per Pattern** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Select the Pattern that its texture to be scaled as the **Gizmo** is activated on the right top corner of the 3D window. \- Click and drag the diagonal arrow. \- The texture will be scaled, maintaining its height and width ratio. \- Click and drag the vertical or horizontal arrow to vertically or horizontally scale the texture respectively. * **Scale per Fabric** \- Select the fabric item to be edited in the Object Browser. \- Navigate and type in desired values to Property Editor ▶**Texture Transformation** ▶ **Width or Height ** ※ Note: **Width** and **Height** can also be adjusted with **Percentage****(%)**(ver5.0.0.)** ** **Rotate Grainline** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mzeXa35c8UI** * **On Pattern** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click on the Pattern that its grainline to be rotated. \- The selected Pattern’s grainline will be activated as it appears in black. \- Click and drag to rotate the grainline. \- The selected Pattern’s grainline and its texture will be rotated towards the direction the mouse was moved. * **In Property Editor** \- Select the Pattern that its grainline to be rotated. \- Navigate and type in desired values to Property Editor ▶ Fabric ▶ **Grainline Direction** \- Once Simulation is activated, the drape will change accordingly. **Rotate** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0AYI2DD2a94 \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022191168/mceclip0.png) **Edit Texture (3D)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click on the Pattern that its texture to be edited. \- When the **Gizmo** tool is activated on the right top corner of the 3D window, click and drag the curved line of the **Gizmo** tool. \- Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to rotate the texture by 45° or 90°. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions and video tutorials for editing 3D textures, including translation, scaling, and rotation techniques to enhance pattern design in CLO 3D.

title: Snap to Grid
content: **List of Contents** Snap to Grid Set Grid Size **Objective** Draft or modify Patterns and Internal Shapes using grids. ** Location** **Snap to Grid** Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **Snap to Grid** (ver3.2 or earlier) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Snap to Grid** (ver3.2 or ealier) Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties (F12) ▶ 2D Grid ▶ **Snap to Grid** (ver4.0 or later) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D/2D Window) ▶ Grid Properties (F12) ▶ 2D Grid ▶ **Snap to Grid** (ver4.0 or later) **Set Grid Size** Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **2D Pattern Window Properties/ Grid Properties**(ver3.2 or earlier) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **2D Pattern Window Properties/ Grid Properties**(ver3.2 or earlier) Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ Grid Properties (F12) ▶ 2D Grid ▶ **Distance** (ver4.0 or later) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D/2D Window) ▶ Grid Properties (F12) ▶ 2D Grid ▶ **Distance** (ver4.0 or later) ** Operation** **Snap to Grid** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **Snap to Grid** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **Snap to Grid** → Patterns and Internal Shapes snap to the grids when moved. **Set Grid Size** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **2D Pattern Window Properties/ Grid Properties**(ver4.0.0) Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ **2D Pattern Window Properties/ Grid Properties**(ver4.0.0) 2. Find the **Distance** option in the Property Editor. 3. Enter the desired value. →The grid reflects the change. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides instructions for utilizing the Snap to Grid and Set Grid Size features to effectively draft or modify patterns and internal shapes using grids.

title: Select All With Same Property
content: **List of Contents** Select All with Same Property Select All with Same Property from Pop-Up Menu Select All with Same Property from Property Editor **Select All with Same Property** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1v-5LeK8_Y \- Select all Patterns will the same property. \- Right-click on the Pattern and select **Select All with Same Property** from the pop-up menu, or select the same option in the property editor. ** Selected All with Same Property from Pop-Up Menu** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dnGMbouVzXg ** * **Particle Distance** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022656308/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over **Select All with Same Property** and select **Particle Distance** from the pop-up menu. \- All Patterns with the same particle distance will be selected. * **Layer ** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022656308/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over **Select All with Same Property** and select **Layer** from the pop-up menu. \- All Patterns with the same layer will be selected. * **Fabric** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022656308/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on the desired Pattern. Hover the mouse over **Select All with Same Property** and select **Fabric** from the pop-up menu. \- All Patterns with the same fabric will be selected. **Select All with Same Property from Property Editor** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i_-NtbHaC8s \- Select the Pattern from the 2D window. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and find **Simulation Properties.** Right-click on the options below the Simulation Properties. content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to use the "Select All with Same Property" feature in CLO 3D, including step-by-step instructions and instructional videos for selecting patterns based on properties such as particle distance, layer, and fabric.

title: Create Smooth Curve
content: **List of Contents** Smooth Curve Smooth Curve Smooth Curve with Specific Value Smooth Curve with Reference Line **Smooth CurveYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6pSCiC-95h0** \- Round corners of Patterns or Internal Shapes. \- Select the ![Toolbar_2D_Curve_RoundCorner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002351068/Toolbar_2D_Curve_RoundCorner.png)**Smooth Curve** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Main Menu > 2D Pattern > Edit > ![Toolbar_2D_Curve_RoundCorner.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360002351068/Toolbar_2D_Curve_RoundCorner.png)**Smooth Curve** **Smooth CurveYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oxLNHvTO_08** \- Hover the mouse over the corner which you wish to curve. \- Click and drag the corner to convert it to a rounded corner. **Smooth Curve with Specific ValueYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aEXwPAEMTlk** \- To assign a specific length to the rounded corner, right click on the 2D window while click and dragging the desired corner. \- The Round Corner by Length window appears. \- Type in the line length or adjust the curvature. \- Click OK to complete the rounded corner. **Smooth Curve with Reference LineYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YwyPQN-Q47g** \- Click Pattern Outlines that make a corner which needs to be rounded. \- A reference line is created between the selected Pattern Outlines. \- Select the side that needs to be rounded. \- Click and drag the reference line to create the desired curve line. Once you release the mouse, the selected side of the Pattern Outline is replaced with the reference line. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore how to effectively use the Smooth Curve tool in Clo3D for rounding corners and creating precise curve designs in your 2D patterns.

title: [Tool] Seamline Topstitch
content: ### Objective Create a Seamline Topstitch. **Location** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ **Seamline Topstitch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670348/__________.png) **Seamline Topstitch** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Topstitch ▶ **Seamline Topstitch** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005670348/__________.png) **Seamline Topstitch** → All sewing lines on the Pattern are displayed. 2. Click on a point where a Topstitch begins. 3. Move mouse to the direction where the Topstitch is going to be created. 4. Click on another point where the Topstitch ends. → The Topstitch is now being created with being highlighted. **※ Note:** * Click and drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments (ver3.2.0). * Use [lasso selection](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004324447) to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on (ver3.2.0). * OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated (ver3.2.0). * Right click when creating the Topstitch to enter specific length (ver4.2.0).
content_description: Learn how to create and apply Seamline Topstitches in your designs using the Clo3D software.

title: [Style Property] Topstitch Offset (Inch)
content: ### **Objective** Adjust the interval between Topstitches on Internal Lines or Pattern outlines. ** Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Offset** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Offset** 2. Adjust the interval. → The value is now being adjusted and applied. **※ Note :** Offset value appears in inch(in) and this unit of length can be set in millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm) in the User Setting. When alteration is made in inch(in), it automatically appears in millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm) and vice versa. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005620527/____95.png)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for adjusting the interval between Topstitches on Internal Lines or Pattern outlines using the Topstitch Property Editor.

title: Layer Clone (Over)
content: **Layer Clone (Over)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aX8rz_DrydA \- Duplicate a Pattern in its draped state and place it directly over the original Pattern. Sewing Lines will be automatically applied to the Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to connect the cloned Pattern to the original Pattern. \- The Layer Clone (Under) function is efficient when creating a double-layered Garment such as padding, collar, cuffs, and more. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform pattern** tool or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and right click on the Pattern to be cloned and select **Layer Clone (Over)** from the pop-up menu. \- The cloned Pattern will follow along the mouse. Click on the 2D window to place the cloned Pattern. \- In the 3D window, the cloned Pattern will be directly placed over the original Pattern and its Pattern outlines and Internal Lines will be sewn to the original Pattern. \- The cloned Patterns will be highlighted in light green in the 2D window and the linked editing will be applied.
content_description: Discover how to efficiently duplicate and layer patterns in CLO 3D using the Layer Clone (Over) and Layer Clone (Under) functions for enhanced garment design.

title: Strengthen/Unstrengthen
content: **Objective** The Pattern Strengthen is a feature that temporarily applies hard properties to the garment. When a pattern is folded, it can be folded more reliably by receiving a strong force from the line segment applied with the folding angle and if a garment is simulated by overlapping each other, it can be solved by simulating flat with the rigid force of the physical properties. **Location** 3D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490267/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005490287/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png) **Transform Pattern** **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the 3D or 2D pattern and click the **Strengthen/Unstrengthen**. → The pattern will be strengthened/unstrengthened. **※Note:** Right-click on the background of the 3D window and hover **Show/Hide Color** **▶** Click the Show **Strengthen** Menu to show or hide the color applied during strengthening. (ver 6.1)
content_description: Discover how to enhance garment simulation accuracy by utilizing the Pattern Strengthen feature, which temporarily applies hard properties for more reliable folding and overlapping in CLO 3D design.

title: Synchronize Pattern
content: **Objective** **ver2.3.0** All adjustments made in the 2D window **automatically** synchronizes with the 3D window. Simulation automatically ends when making a modification on 2D Pattern while simulating. **ver2.2.0** Once the sync button is activating, any adjustments, not only design adjustments, but also sewing lines, print textures, particle distances get reflected in the 3D window. Even if the synchronization is off, activating the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005481127/Toolbar_3D_Simulation.png) **Simulation** tool auto-activates the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** tool and reflects on the 3D window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ **Sync** (Ctrl + D) 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** (Ctrl + D) ### **Operation** 1\. Make adjustments in the 2D window. 2\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ **Sync** (Ctrl + D) 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005529108/___.png) **Sync** (Ctrl + D) **※ Note:****** **Changes in a Pattern Color According to Synchronization** A Pattern that has never been synchronized appears in transparent. A Pattern that has been synchronized at least once appears in red color, and a Pattern that its synchronization is currently activating appears in blue color.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on synchronizing adjustments between the 2D and 3D windows in version 2.3.0 of the software, ensuring real-time updates and enhanced design accuracy.

content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to applying grading and size groups in pattern design, complete with instructional videos and step-by-step instructions for creating, applying, and managing size groups.

title: Particle Distance Setting
content: ### **Objective** Particle Distance refers to the average distance between the points that make up a Garment Pattern, in other words, size of the mesh. The Garment quality and Simulation speed depend on the Particle Distance. Therefore set the value at 20mm when making a Garment and dressing it on an Avatar for faster working process, and set it under 5mm to enhance the Garment quality once it is completed. **Location** Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Particle Distance** **Operation** 1. Select Pattern(s). 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Particle Distance ** 3. Input desired value for the Particle Distance. (Minimum '0.8' to maximum '700.0') 4. Press Enter on keyboard to apply.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on optimizing Particle Distance settings in garment simulation to balance quality and efficiency in design.
